design.title: Probe first, then fine-tune: one extra opening epoch trains only the head on the FROZEN ImageNet trunk, so the random tile head's first gradients cannot distort the borrowed eyes (LP-FT)
design.init_strategy: pretrained:efficientnet_b0 IMAGENET1K_V1 features[0..7] (torchvision, Apache-2.0 weights), head linear-probed on the frozen trunk for 1 epoch, then fine-tuned at 0.1x LR
design.eli5: The model's 'eyes' were borrowed from a network that had already looked at a million everyday photos, and that borrowed vision is what lets it recognise Berlin in a photograph it has never seen. Until now we started teaching the eyes and the brand-new 'map-reading' part at the same moment — so in the first hours the confused new part was yanking the borrowed eyes around. Now the map-reading part first practises for one round with the eyes held still, and only then are both tuned together, so the eyes keep more of what made them useful.
design.hypothesis: Every large step on the held-out truedop_2024 photograph in this era came from the ImageNet-pretrained trunk (exp 12: 10.75% -> 49.5% usable; exp 16 MobileNetV2: 86.75%; exp 19 EfficientNet-B0: 92.5%), i.e. what transfers to a never-seen survey is the invariance the trunk brought from a million photographs, not what it learned from three. Experiment 20 (champion, 0.078: usable 93.0%, false 0.75%, abstain 6.25%) shows that how the trunk is TRAINED still matters out-of-domain: a better point on the same trajectory bought 0.5 points of usable and cut false fixes from 1.0% to 0.75% while the three training photographs stayed at 100%. The size gate (31.7 MB of 33.6 MB) closes the capacity road, so the remaining lever is the fine-tuning procedure. Today the trunk is fine-tuned from step 1 jointly with a RANDOMLY INITIALISED head (prototypes std 0.01 over 2,970 tiles, random 1x1 lifts, random embed BatchNorm): the earliest, largest gradients reaching the pretrained blocks are noise from a head that does not yet know any tile, and their trunk BatchNorm running stats start adapting at the same moment. Kumar et al. (ICLR 2022, 'Fine-Tuning can Distort Pretrained Features and Underperform Out-of-Distribution') prove and measure exactly this: full fine-tuning from a random head distorts the pretrained features along the directions the in-domain data uses and leaves the rest behind, which costs out-of-distribution accuracy (~7-10 points OOD on their benchmarks) while in-distribution accuracy is unchanged or better; training the head first on the frozen trunk (linear probe, then fine-tune: LP-FT) removes most of that loss. That is our split precisely: in-domain saturated at 100%, out-of-domain at 93%. Nothing in this era (searched hypothesis/method for freeze/probe/warm-up: none) nor in the 83 earlier experiments ever trained the head before the trunk; the trunk's training procedure since exp 12 has been 'fine-tune at 0.1x from step 1' unchanged. Builds on experiment 20 (the champion) with architecture, graph, losses, augmentation, MixStyle, committee, the fine-tune schedule and weight averaging all unchanged.
